cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, has just counted every man twenty and older who can serve in the army (Numbers 1:2-3). That's a LOT of people, friend. Now the LORD speaks to Moses and his brother Aaron (Exodus 4:14), and the big question is: where do you PUT everybody?

cards.question: The LORD tells the Israelites to camp all the way around something. What sits at the center of it all?
True or false: the LORD tells the tribes to pitch their tents right up against the Tent of Meeting.

cards.text: They camp at a distance, each man under his standard, with the banners of his family. In my junk drawer we didn't have banners. We had a takeout menu and a rubber band, and we were GRATEFUL.

cards.question: The LORD starts with the east side of the camp, toward the sunrise. Which tribe's divisions camp there?

cards.text: Judah's leader is Nahshon son of Amminadab, and his division alone is 74,600 men. Issachar and Zebulun camp right next to them, so the east side is PACKED like a cookie box on a holiday.

cards.question: The camp of Judah has 186,400 men in all. When Israel moves, the LORD says they shall set out ___.

cards.text: South side: the camp of Reuben, led by Elizur son of Shedeur, with Simeon and Gad beside them. That's 151,450 men setting out second, and second is FINE, friend, I spent years at the back of a drawer.
Okay, east and south are set. But before the LORD gets to the other two sides, He talks about the middle. The part everybody's camped around.

cards.question: When Israel is on the move, who travels with the Tent of Meeting in the middle of the camps?
True or false: when they set out, each tribe travels in the same order it camped, in its own place under its standard.

cards.text: West side: the camp of Ephraim, led by Elishama son of Ammihud, with Manasseh and Benjamin beside them. That's 108,100 men setting out third, and I have officially run out of mustache to count on.
That leaves one side. The north. Somebody's getting it, and I'm sitting here like it's the last cookie on the tray.

cards.question: Three tribes are left, and all three camp on the north side. Which tribe's standard do they camp under?

cards.text: Dan's leader is Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai, and Asher and Naphtali camp beside them. That's 157,600 men setting out LAST, and hey, somebody's gotta turn off the oven on the way out.

cards.question: True or false: with the camp of Dan setting out last, the Tent of Meeting travels at the very back, right behind them.

cards.text: Add it all up and you get 603,550 men. SIX. HUNDRED. THOUSAND. Friend, I used to get nervous when six cookie cutters shared one counter.

cards.question: True or false: the Levites, who travel with the Tent of Meeting, are counted in that total of 603,550.
So how do the Israelites handle the LORD's plan for camping and setting out?

answers.text: They follow only part of it
They swap a few of the spots

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: 'They camp at a distance...', 'In my junk drawer we didn't have banners.' and 'We had a takeout menu and a rubber band, and we were GRATEFUL.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't share the core action of the fact. In 2:2, each man camps under his standard with his family's banners, which is about belonging to a marked group. A takeout menu and a rubber band 'and we were GRATEFUL' doesn't match that action, so a reader could say 'huh?' about why they'd be grateful or what the items stand in for.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: Asher and Naphtali are arguable as answers. Verse 2 says 'each man under his standard,' verse 17 says 'each in his own place under his standard,' and verse 31 says the camp of Dan sets out 'under their standards' (plural). A baker could argue that Asher's men camp under Asher's standard. The answers are also exactly the three north tribes, none of which the baker has been told about, so the pick comes down to luck.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The line 'I used to get nervous when six cookie cutters shared one counter' adds something new to his backstory, and it contradicts it. In the backstory, the cutters were the nervous ones and Papa Dorin was the one who calmed them. This moment is set in the Millers' kitchen, not his bakery.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: Written with periods, 'SIX. HUNDRED. THOUSAND.' makes this story card read as 5 sentences. It also has 3 sentences even if that phrase is counted as one.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Almost all of Numbers 2 is a census and a camp layout: four camps, each with a lead tribe, a leader, the tribes beside it, division counts, a total and its order for setting out. The walkthrough treats the leaders and numbers as a summarized stretch, but it puts choice cards on which tribe camps on which side (cards 5 and 14) and on the setting-out order (card 7). The docs list 'census counts and numbers' and 'land boundaries and town lists' as long stretches, which never get choice cards. They don't say what to do when the whole passage is that kind of material, or whether a camp layout counts as a long stretch at all.
findings.question: When a whole passage is mostly a census or arrangement list, like Numbers 2, does it count as a long stretch? Can the arrangement itself (which tribe leads each side, the order for setting out) get choice cards while only the leaders and counts are summarized?
